Project Name: AI & Digital Twin Integrated Control Platform for Pathogen Monitoring
Short Description: Developed an integrated infection-control platform that uses AI and digital twins to detect, analyze, monitor and control infectious disease spread in hospitals in real time, demonstrated at Osong Bestian Hospital.
Long Description:
Background & Goals
A project carried out under the 2026 Digital Twin Leading Program for AI-based Safety Management by NIA (National Information Society Agency). Led by X2R with UNIST, Cheongju University, WOSEM and Bestian Hospital, the K-AI Quarantine Control Consortium developed an integrated platform that detects infectious disease spread inside hospitals in real time and connects it to analysis, monitoring and control. The platform was installed and operated at Osong Bestian Hospital to validate its performance, laying the groundwork for expansion to other medical institutions and public facilities.

Key Features
  • 3D digital twin monitoring — The entire hospital rebuilt in realistic 3D, showing negative pressure, temperature/humidity and pathogen detection by floor and room on a single screen
  • Airflow simulation — CFD analysis of room airflow and contamination spread, predicting whether negative pressure is reached at given supply/exhaust rates
  • Real-time IoT integration — Links SERS pathogen sensors, negative-pressure units, thermal cameras and wearables, automatically controlling negative-pressure equipment by risk level
  • Antechamber visitor monitoring — Thermal cameras track foot traffic and febrile visitors, AI forecasts visitor numbers, and data is linked in real time with the KDCA infectious disease feed
  • AI rounding routes — AI-recommended rounding routes, with negative-pressure switching during rounds to block contamination leaks
Demonstration Site
The full detect → analyze → monitor → control cycle was demonstrated at Osong Bestian Hospital, in the 1st-floor antechamber (thermal and questionnaire screening) and the 5th-floor ward (automatic negative-pressure control).

Technology
  • Digital twin — Equipment, spaces and processes are replicated in a virtual space and linked to real data, reflecting their current state in real time.
  • CFD airflow simulation — Computational fluid dynamics calculates room airflow, visualizing contamination paths and whether negative pressure is achieved.
  • SERS pathogen sensors — Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy sensors detect airborne viruses on site and send results to the platform in real time.
  • Thermal cameras — Visitor numbers and body temperature are measured without contact, quickly identifying foot traffic and febrile visitors.
  • AI analytics & prediction — Models trained on accumulated data detect anomalies or forecast what comes next, supporting on-site decision-making.
  • Public infectious disease data — Infectious disease data from the KDCA is received in real time and shown alongside on-site monitoring.
